text:
maya: FYI eviction spike noticed on the spot pool in us-west1 this morning (06:00-08:00 UTC). Interactive pods experienced higher tail latency.
jorge: Confirmed. Looks like a mix of scheduled maintenance and transient price pressure. Eviction rate ≈ 12% on gpu-t4 nodes for that window.
li: We move a lot of batch to us-east1 overnight. Interactive traffic is global; when we fallback to on-demand across regions p99 suffers. Need smarter regional placement.
sam: Short-term mitigation: create a small on-demand warm pool per region for interactive. Prefer those for binding. If exhausted, allow interactive onto spot but reduce KV-cache TTL.
elena: Also, avoid cross-region rescheduling for interactive — egress cost + latency kill p99. Keep fallbacks region-local only.
infra-bot: alert: spot-eviction-rate(us-west1,gpu-t4) > 10% (30m window)
maya: Could we try an off-peak spot-rotation to shift bids/capacity overnight while keeping a small warm on-demand pool to soak interactive spikes?
jorge: Proposed pattern:
- Two nodepools per region: spot-bulk (cheap) + on-demand-warm (small, steady)
- Autoscaler scales spot-bulk for batch workloads; interactive pods bind to on-demand-warm first
- Interactive allowed onto spot only with a lower scheduling priority and a PREFER_ON_DEMAND taint
- Canary in a single region for 48h before global roll-out
li: Checkpointing is required for batch. For long-running jobs, 5-10m checkpoint intervals. Short micro-batches can use ephemeral caching.
elena: Add an eviction handler sidecar that reacts to SIGTERM and flushes KV/cache to S3 within ~30s. In testing that preserved ~90% of warm state compared to hard kills.
sam: Example preStop snippet we use in pods:
```
preStop: "/usr/local/bin/evict-flush.sh"
# evict-flush.sh -> flush local KV, push metadata to s3, sleep 10
```
maya: Remember interactive SLO: 200ms p99 for short prompts. Batch tolerates ~30s. Scheduler needs to encode those SLOs as queue priorities.
jorge: We'll add kube-scheduler policies + queue priorities in job-runner (high=interactive, med=short-batch, low=elastic-batch). Also gang-scheduling for multi-GPU runs.
li: Cost analysis: raw spot saves ~60-70%, but interruptions and retries add ~5-12% extra cost. We need guardrails that flip to on-demand if effective_cost > on-demand.
elena: Agree. Define effective_cost = (spot_price + retry_overhead) / availability_factor and compare to on-demand baseline. Optimizer should route accordingly.
maya: I'll prototype a cron-based spot-rotation PoC that adjusts bid caps at 03:00 UTC (off-peak) and tracks eviction delta. @jorge, can you take autoscaler/taint tuning?
jorge: I got autoscaler and taint rules. I'll canary in us-east1 for 48h and post metrics back here.
sam: I'll publish an eviction-sidecar image and add the preStop script to the model base image.
li: I'll extend job-runner with a --checkpoint-interval flag and expose queue priority knobs to the scheduler.
elena: I'll add dashboard panels and alerts: spot_evictions(region), effective_cost_estimate, on_demand_pressure.
infra-bot: deploy: spot-rotation-poc started by maya (canary region: us-east1) at 1753050000
maya: Action items recap:
- maya: deploy spot-rotation cron (03:00 UTC), monitor 72h
- jorge: autoscaler + taint policy + on-demand warm pool (canary 48h)
- sam: eviction-sidecar + preStop image
- li: job-runner checkpointing + queue priorities
- elena: eviction metrics + dashboard panels
maya: If eviction_rate > 8% after changes, revert rotation and scale up warm on-demand capacity. Add rollback steps to the runbook.
jorge: I'll draft an emergency runbook (kubectl patch nodepool, force drain, increase on-demand count) and post it.
li: Adding a guard in the optimizer: if retry_overhead pushes effective_cost above on-demand for 1h, switch bidding strategy to conservative.
elena: I'll create alerting: spot_evictions(region) > 8% for 30m -> paging + auto-disable rotation in that region.
maya: Thanks team :thumbsup: Reconvene in 48h with canary metrics to decide next steps.
